content:
For the first time, New York City’s massive Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, as the city and region prepare for an approaching nor’easter.

The 100th annual parade, originally scheduled for Thursday, will now run on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET. Crews had already filled the parade’s fleet with helium in preparation for the march at the time of the Wednesday announcement, according to the New York Post.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s said in a statement obtained by WABC-TV.

At a press conference on Wednesday evening, Mayor Zohran Mamdani emphasized the dangers of the incoming weather and asked New Yorkers to be prepared.

“Now I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” said Mamdani, who will not be able to attend the rescheduled parade because of a planned surgery. “I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences. Yet safety has to come first. And on Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe.”

The delay comes as the East Coast prepares for major rainstorms around the holiday, with the National Weather Service saying wind gusts could reach 60 mph on Thanksgiving Day — far above the city’s 34 mph threshold for the parade to fly its balloons.

High wind warnings for the area are rare, with NWS reporting that only 37 have been issued in the last 24 years for the city.

Thursday could also be New York City’s wettest Thanksgiving Day in at least two decades. The East Coast is expected to face the highest water levels since Superstorm Sandy, while parts of Delaware and New Jersey could deal with power outage risks from strong winds.

“I’ve declared a statewide State of emergency, effective at 6:00 PM today, ahead of a powerful coastal storm. Damaging winds, heavy rain and severe tidal flooding are expected through Friday, with the most dangerous conditions on Thanksgiving Day,” New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill posted on X.

“Be prepared for prolonged power outages, detours, and road closures,” she continued. “Please travel today if possible, charge your devices, and never drive through flooded roadways.”

The East Coast is not the only region facing severe weather during the holiday, when AAA estimates tens of millions of people will be traveling. High tides known as “king tides,” combined with powerful waves, have already begun flooding some California communities, destroying part of a pier in the northern city of Pacifica.

Taiyler S. Mitchell contributed to this story.
